body.statement:
The structural direct effect \(\beta\) is point-identified relative to \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) at every parameter with \(r^\star<\infty\), without requiring \(r^\star\leq R_{\max}\).  More precisely, for every integer \(k\geq d+2\) such that \(Q_Ac_k\neq0\),
\[
 \beta=
 \frac{\langle Q_Ac_k,Q_Am_k\rangle}
      {\lVert Q_Ac_k\rVert_2^2}.
\]
On the bounded legal-swap domain \(\mathcal D_\rho\), \(\beta\) is identified if and only if \(r^\star<\infty\).  Indeed, every \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho\) and \(S\theta\) induce the same collection \(\{P_e:e\in\mathcal E\}\), both belong to \(\mathcal D_\rho\), and their effects are the distinct numbers \(\beta\) and \(\beta+\gamma/\alpha\).  The positive result is a statement about the new low-rank population flag class, not about arbitrary simultaneous source shifts.
body.proof_tex:
The causal target is the coefficient \(\beta\), rather than a definition made from observed cumulants.  Under an intervention setting treatment to \(t\), while holding the exogenous variables fixed, the outcome equation becomes
\[
 Y_e(t)=\beta t+\gamma U_e+\epsilon_y.
 \tag{6}
\]
Thus replacing \(t\) by \(t+1\) changes the potential outcome by \(\beta\); this establishes the causal meaning of the target independently of the observable functional below.

Let \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) and suppose \(r^\star<\infty\).  By the definition of the first breakout, there is an integer \(k\geq d+2\) for which \(Q_Ac_k\neq0\).  The population cumulant-cancellation lemma gives
\[
 Q_Am_k=\beta Q_Ac_k.
 \tag{7}
\]
Taking the Euclidean inner product of (7) with \(Q_Ac_k\) gives
\[
 \langle Q_Ac_k,Q_Am_k\rangle
 =\beta\lVert Q_Ac_k\rVert_2^2.
 \tag{8}
\]
The denominator in (8) is strictly positive because \(Q_Ac_k\neq0\), so division is valid and yields the displayed quotient.

Every object on the right side is determined by the observed laws.  Specifically, the finite moments guaranteed by \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) determine the cumulants and hence \(c_k,m_k\); the observed contrasts \(c_2,\ldots,c_{d+1}\) determine \(C\); the rank condition \(\operatorname{rank}(C)=d\) makes \(C^\top C\) invertible; and the projector definition then determines \(Q_A\).  Now let \(\widetilde\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) induce the same collection of observed laws as \(\theta\).  It has the same \(c_j,m_j,C,Q_A\) for every \(j\), so it has the same finite \(r^\star\).  Applying (8) to \(\widetilde\theta\) gives
\[
 \widetilde\beta
 =\frac{\langle Q_Ac_k,Q_Am_k\rangle}
        {\lVert Q_Ac_k\rVert_2^2}
 =\beta.
\]
This proves point identification relative to the broad population class.  No order cap was used.

We next restrict attention to \(\mathcal D_\rho\).  The definition of the bounded ambient class makes \(\Theta\subseteq\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\).  Hence every \(\theta\in\mathcal B\), for which \(d+2\leq r^\star\leq R_{\max}\), is covered by the preceding identification argument, even against every observationally equivalent alternative in the larger class \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\).

Let instead \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho\).  The treatment-loading bound gives \(|\alpha|\geq a_0>0\), so define
\[
 V_e=\alpha\epsilon_{u,e},
 \qquad W_e=\epsilon_{t,e},
 \qquad q=\frac{\gamma}{\alpha}.
\]
The structural equations then read
\[
 T_e=V_e+W_e,
 \qquad
 Y_e=(\beta+q)V_e+\beta W_e+\epsilon_y.
 \tag{9}
\]
Under the source swap, the latent and treatment sources are respectively \(W_e\) and \(V_e\), while the coefficients are \(1,\beta+q,-q\).  Consequently its observables satisfy
\[
 T'_e=W_e+V_e=T_e,
\]
and
\[
 Y'_e=(\beta+q)(W_e+V_e)-qW_e+\epsilon_y
      =(\beta+q)V_e+\beta W_e+\epsilon_y=Y_e.
 \tag{10}
\]
Thus the swap preserves the complete observed law in every environment, not merely the displayed cumulants.

By definition of \(\mathcal N_\rho\), both \(\theta\) and \(S\theta\) are in \(\Theta_\rho^\circ\) and both have infinite breakout.  To verify that the alternative itself belongs to \(\mathcal N_\rho\), compute
\[
 S^2\theta=
 \left(1,\beta,\frac{\gamma}{\alpha},
       \{\alpha\epsilon_{u,e},\epsilon_{t,e}\}_{e\in\mathcal E},
       \epsilon_y\right).
 \tag{11}
\]
The loading \(1\) is interior because it is already the loading of \(S\theta\); the effect \(\beta\) and confounding ratio \(\gamma/\alpha\) inherit the interior bounds of \(\theta\).  The two source families in (11) are the two source families of \(S\theta\) in reverse order, so centeredness, mutual independence, all-order moment existence, and the finite moment envelope are inherited from \(S\theta\).  The latent shift at order \(k\) in (11) is \(\alpha^ku_k\), which belongs to \(A\) because \(u_k\in A\).  Equations (9)--(10), applied once more, show that its observed laws, calibration matrix, calibration gap, and infinite breakout equal those of \(\theta\).  Hence \(S^2\theta\in\Theta_\rho^\circ\) and \(r^\star(S^2\theta)=\infty\).  The definition of the no-breakout branch now gives
\[
 S\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho\subseteq\mathcal D_\rho.
\]

Finally, the two effects differ by \(q=\gamma/\alpha\).  The confounding bound gives \(|q|\geq q_0>0\), so they are distinct.  Since two parameters in \(\mathcal D_\rho\) with the same observed laws have different causal targets, no observed-law functional identifies \(\beta\) at a point of \(\mathcal N_\rho\).  Since \(\mathcal D_\rho=\mathcal B\cup\mathcal N_\rho\), identification holds there exactly on the finite-breakout branch.  The broad positive result used only membership in \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\), whereas the negative result used the explicit bounded legal-swap restriction; this proves the two scopes stated in the theorem.
body.justification: This theorem separates unrestricted-order population identification from bounded inference and legal-swap nonidentification: any finite orthogonal cumulant flag identifies the structural effect in the new low-rank population class.
body.gap: Kivva et al., Theorem 3.6, gives a simultaneous-shift obstruction in a two-environment setting. It does not provide the projected-plane recovery map or identification at an arbitrary finite breakout in this new calibrated multi-environment submodel.
body.consumer: For a selected edge in the Sachs perturbation panel, the theorem returns a direct-effect functional whenever the maintained population profile has a finite flag, while the bounded no-breakout branch reports an exact source-label ambiguity.
